## Dimensioning Rules {#dimensioningrules} ### Learning Objectives {-} By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: - Apply fundamental dimensioning rules according to ASME Y14.5 standards - Select appropriate dimension placement for clarity and manufacturability - Use proper extension lines, dimension lines, and leaders - Dimension common features including holes, arcs, and angles - Avoid common dimensioning errors ::: {.callout-think} **Before You Read:** Look at any mechanical part near you. How would you communicate its exact size to someone who needs to manufacture it? What measurements would be most important? ::: ### Introduction to Dimensioning Dimensioning is the process of adding size and location information to engineering drawings. Proper dimensioning ensures that parts can be manufactured exactly as the designer intended. ::: {.callout-industry} **Industry Connection:** In the defense industry, improper dimensioning can have serious consequences. A famous example is the Mars Climate Orbiter, which was lost due to a unit conversion error. Clear dimensioning standards prevent such costly mistakes. ::: ### Try it yourself {#sec-tryit-dimensioning} ```{=html}
``` ### Key Takeaways {-} - Dimensions should be placed for maximum clarity - Each dimension should appear only once on a drawing - Dimensions should relate to functional requirements - Standard symbols and conventions ensure universal understanding ::: {.callout-check} **Quick Check:** What is the difference between an extension line and a dimension line? Why is it important not to dimension to hidden lines? :::
